transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I've been having some trouble with how much I'm eating. 

Especially after my late shifts at work, I'll stop for takeout on the way home and end up eating, you know, two burgers, fries, and a shake. But then I still go home and clean out the leftovers we keep out in the garage fridge, almost like it's a second supper. It's just a lot of food, and I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
After you eat this much, do you ever try to get rid of the food or 'make up for it'—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising intensely?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never tried to make myself throw up or used laxatives or anything like that. And I'm definitely not exercising—by the time I finish a long shift and eat all that, I'm way too tired to work out. I mostly just end up going to sleep feeling completely stuffed and... well, pretty miserable about it. But no, I don't try to get rid of it.
During these episodes of eating a lot of food, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating once you start?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start, it feels like a switch is flipped. I'll actually be sitting there telling myself, you know, "Roy, shut the bag and go inside," but... I just can't. My hands just keep reaching for more. It's like I have absolutely no control over it once I get going.
How often would you say these episodes of feeling out of control while eating happen—like, how many times per week—and how many weeks or months has this been going on?

Well, I'd say this has been going on for the past few months now. As for how often... there's usually at least one night a week where I end up doing this. But honestly, it's often two or three times a week. 

It really just depends on work. If I've had a rough day on the line, or if I'm pulling a lot of those late shifts, that's when it usually happens. So yeah, probably two or three times a week for a few months.
After these episodes, do you feel disgusted with yourself, guilty, or depressed about how much you ate?

Yeah, I do. Afterward, I feel... well, ashamed, mostly. And kind of disgusted with myself. I've always thought of myself as a pretty disciplined guy, you know? Dependable. I go to work, I do my job. But when this happens... it makes me feel like I'm sneaking around. Like I'm just completely letting myself down.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient endorses recurrent binge eating episodes (2-3x/week, some weeks only 1x/week) characterized by eating large amounts of food with a subjective sense of loss of control, eating despite not being hungry (garage fridge leftovers after already eating a large fast-food meal), and marked distress/guilt/shame following episodes. No compensatory behaviors (no vomiting, laxative use, or compensatory exercise) are present, ruling out bulimia nervosa. However, the reported duration ('past few months') does not clearly establish the required 3-month minimum duration with consistent weekly frequency needed for a full Binge-Eating Disorder diagnosis, and no data was obtained regarding additional associated features (eating rapidly, eating alone due to embarrassment, feeling uncomfortably full) required to confirm at least 3 of 5 associated behavioral indicators. Given a clinically significant binge-eating pattern with associated distress that does not yet meet full syndromal criteria for BED, this is best classified as an Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder (subthreshold binge-eating disorder).
